s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions first appeared on cheeks
Lesions have gradually coalesced
Lesion size ranges from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No symptoms reported
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with congenital or acquired hypopigmented lesions

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Common condition presenting with hypopigmented patches, often on face

shortlist.label: Tuberous sclerosis complex
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings of subepidermal tumor and glycogen accumulation are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Vitiligo
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules, although typically with sharper borders

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, with a 2-year history and no symptoms, matches the typical clinical features of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Nevus depigmentosus typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented patch, which does not match the patient's multiple lesions.

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Pityriasis alba is a condition that typically affects children and is characterized by ill-defined, faintly hypopigmented patches, often with a scaling surface, which does not fit the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Tuberous sclerosis complex
rejected.why: Tuberous sclerosis complex is a genetic disorder that presents with a range of systemic and cutaneous manifestations, including ash-leaf spots, shagreen patches, and adenoma sebaceum, which are not mentioned in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Vitiligo is characterized by well-defined, depigmented patches, often with a distinct border, which does not match the patient's hypopigmented macules with gradual coalescence.
